I am an old woman now, 71 years, but this maize plot on the slopes here in Kilimanjaro has fed my family for many seasons. The volcanic soil is good, and I intercrop my maize with beans as my mother taught me — the beans help the soil and feed us when maize is short. I will buy a little DAP and urea from the agrodealer in town if the price is not too high, and I still keep manure from my few cattle to spread on the plot. My grandchildren help me in the field, but my back is not strong, so I must hire some young men for ploughing and weeding.
